title: Invertible modules form an open substack for proper flat algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to S$ a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Let $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ be the category fibred in groupoids of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules on $X_T=X\times_ST$, flat over $T$ with support proper over $T$, with tensor-pullback isomorphisms as arrows, as specified in [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general]. Let $\mathcal L_{X/S}(T)$ be the full groupoid of line modules on $X_T$: modules on its small etale ringed site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Its pullbacks are $u_X^*M=\mathcal O_{X_{T'}}\otimes_{u_X^{-1}\mathcal O_{X_T}}u_X^{-1}M$ [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Forgetting invertibility defines a fully faithful morphism $\mathcal L_{X/S}\to\mathcal C_{X/S}$ representable by open immersions [def-sfb-open-moduli-substack]. Explicitly, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and object $F\in\mathcal C_{X/S}(T)$ there is an open subscheme $U_F\subseteq T$ such that, for every scheme map $v:T'\to T$, $v_X^*F$ is a line module if and only if $v$ factors through $U_F$, and $T\times_{\mathcal C_{X/S}}\mathcal L_{X/S}$ is represented by $U_F$. No Noetherian, reduced-fibre, section or cohomological-flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D03 (lemma-picard-stack-open-in-coh), for algebraic spaces, not only schemes.

proof.text: For each $T\to S$, put $p=f_T:X_T\to T$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $p$ is flat, proper and finitely presented. A line module $L$ has local presentation $\mathcal O^0\to\mathcal O\to L\to0$, hence is quasi-coherent and finitely presented. On these trivializations its flatness over $T$ is that of $\mathcal O_{X_T}$, hence follows from flatness of $p$. Its support is proper: take the closed immersion $X_T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X_T$ and the finite type module $L$ in the support definition of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general]. Thus it is an object of $\mathcal C_{X/S}(T)$. Tensor pullback sends a local generator $e$ to $1\otimes e$, with inverse $a\otimes be\mapsto ab$ on a trivialization. It therefore preserves line modules. On isomorphisms the forgetful functor is the inclusion of a full subgroupoid, so is fully faithful and respects cartesian pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

Fix $F\in\mathcal C_{X/S}(T)$. It is finitely presented, quasi-coherent and flat over $T$ by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general]. The morphism $p:X_T\to T$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-finite-free-locus-base-change] to obtain the open subset $W=W(F)$ of $|X_T|$. For every $v:T'\to T$, writing $q:X_{T'}\to X_T$, its conclusion gives $W(q^*F)=|q|^{-1}(W)$, including for nonflat $v$ and nonreduced test schemes.

Within $W$, let $V$ be the locus of rank one. On an etale trivialization $F\simeq\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ the rank is $r$: two such trivializations have the same rank at a common geometric point because tensoring their isomorphism with its residue field gives an isomorphism of finite-dimensional vector spaces. The images of these etale trivializing charts are open by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], so every rank locus is open in $W$; $V$ is open in $|X_T|$, and $C=|X_T|\setminus V$ is closed. For $q$ as above, step 2 identifies the free loci. At points of this inverse image, pulling back a trivialization gives $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ again; its geometric fibre has dimension $r$ after any residue-field extension. Consequently $V(q^*F)=|q|^{-1}(V)$ and $C(q^*F)=|q|^{-1}(C)$. Here $V(q^*F)$ denotes its rank-one locally free locus, not a support. A module is a line module precisely when this locus is the entire space, by the local definition of line module [def-trf-algebraic-space].

Since $p$ is proper, its map on topological spaces is closed, as explicitly stated in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Define the open subscheme $U_F=T\setminus p(C)$. For any $v:T'\to T$, the set $|q|^{-1}(C)$ is empty exactly when $v$ has image in $U_F$. Indeed a point of $X_{T'}$ over a point of $C$ gives a point of $T'$ mapping into $p(C)$. Conversely, if $t'\in T'$ and $x\in C$ have the same image $t\in T$, represent $x$ by a field-valued point and combine its residue field with $\kappa(t')$ over $\kappa(t)$. The common-extension theorem [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], applied to these two extensions of $\kappa(t)$, supplies a common field with embeddings agreeing on $\kappa(t)$. The two maps from its spectrum therefore give a point of the sheaf fibre product $X_T\times_TT'$ over both. This uses exactly the fibre-product and field-valued-point conventions of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Step 3 now says that $v_X^*F$ is a line module exactly when $v$ has image in $U_F$, equivalently when $v$ factors uniquely through this open subscheme. The same argument allows empty spaces and empty fibres.

Over a map $v:T'\to T$, an object of $T\times_{\mathcal C_{X/S}}\mathcal L_{X/S}$ is a line module $L$ together with an isomorphism $\alpha:L\simeq v_X^*F$. Such an object exists exactly under the condition of step 4. If it exists, every two pairs $(L,\alpha),(L',\alpha')$ have the unique arrow $(\alpha')^{-1}\alpha$ respecting the isomorphisms; in particular their automorphisms are trivial. The fibre groupoid is therefore empty or equivalent to the terminal groupoid, exactly as for the discrete representable functor $h_{U_F}$. Sending a pair to the unique factorization through $U_F$ commutes with pullbacks, and its inverse assigns the pulled-back $F$ with its identity isomorphism. This gives the required representing equivalence. By [def-sfb-open-moduli-substack], the full subcategory is an open substack and its inclusion is representable by open immersions.
